title: Feat(live-doc): makes documentation works on smaller screens

comments.body: @bobylito the select is not super handy with ios

Mobile menu looks a bit too... spacy :)
![2015-11-09_09h57m24](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/11029598/5c6d47b8-86c8-11e5-8447-caaedcf1a7ca.gif)

I would not split the content in two columns that early (800px?). On small screens, each column is really narrow. It is more readable to put text and examples one below the other until we really have a a bigger screen (maybe when we start adding the menu column? 1200px?)

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/11029668/cc03626a-86c8-11e5-9c07-1da435ed6eff.png)

Mobile menu are made for: mobile, and I think it works well on mobile.

For breakpoints, I'm ok like that but feel free to test.

Edit: ok for BP it's far to be perfect! :)

Cool that we are tackling this one.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/123822/11032551/b69df1ec-86dc-11e5-8a9c-2f260339ade4.png)

^^^ Is the gif from @pixelastic still accurate? As for the menu (or the whole webpage), it looks really weird that the text is passing below in full transparency.

I know that's a detail but I guess everyone on mobile will stumble on it and their first impression will somehow be different than if it was done in a different manner.

Can we put an opaque background behind "instantsearch.js" so that it's not doing this?
We have merges because merge :) I think it's not too bad for this time and we'll do better next time :) (we promise)
Yep good @Shipow we can have a git workflow course soon no big deal
